name: LFP battery cells
title: Why A123 Systems went bankrupt, and when LFP batteries won
question: Why did A123 Systems go bankrupt, and when did LFP batteries become viable?
answer: A123 Systems (2001) commercialised lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, went public in 2009 and received a $249M federal grant, then filed for bankruptcy in October 2012 when electric-car demand lagged. CATL (2011) scaled LFP into the EV boom. World EV sales went from tens of thousands in 2011 to millions a year.
verdict_reason: EV volume crossed the scale cell makers needed in the mid-2010s.

constraint.name: Electric-vehicle production volume
constraint.detail: Cell factories need volume to reach their costs; in 2012 there were not enough EVs to fill them.

crossing.text: World EV sales pass about half a million a year (IEA via OWID).
